acme_sre: Hey team, after bumping our dependency to the new Go SDK we started seeing build failures in CI. Local devs are fine, CI fails with:
```
can't load package: package github.com/our-org/our-service: module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2: no matching versions for query \"latest\"
# or sometimes:
cannot find module providing package github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2
```
acme_sre: Our go.mod has `require github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v1.7.0` and I tried `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2` and it didn't resolve. Any ideas?

sam_support: thanks for reporting — can you paste the top of your go.mod and the exact import in code? also which go version & CI runner?

acme_sre: go.mod (sensitive parts removed):
```
module github.com/our-org/our-service

go 1.19

require (
    github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v1.7.0
)
```
imports: `import \"github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2\"` in our client wrapper. CI is linux/go 1.19 on GH actions. Local `go env` same.

maria_eng: this looks like a classic v2 module path/tag mismatch. Major versions >v1 need the module path to include /v2 and the release tags must match (v2.x.y). If the upstream module's go.mod still says `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk` but you import `/v2`, Go treats that as a different module and will try to find `github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2` which must be a module with that exact path.

maria_eng: quick checklist:
- confirm upstream module `go.mod` has `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2` for the v2 series
- confirm upstream tag is `v2.0.0` (or v2.x.y) on the repo (not `v1.0.0` or missing the v2 prefix)
- CI sometimes caches modules; try `go clean -modcache` on the runner or clear cache in actions

acme_sre: we inspected the upstream repo and the latest tag is `v2.0.0` but the repo's go.mod still shows `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk` (no /v2). opa.

maria_eng: that's the root cause — if the tag is v2 but module path is not updated, some clients behave inconsistently. Two common fixes:
1) Upstream: update module path to `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2` and cut a new v2 tag (v2.1.0) that contains that go.mod. This is the correct semantic-go way.
2) Workaround in your repo: use a replace directive to map the v2 import to the v1 module path (temporary):
```
replace github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2 => github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk v2.0.0
```
Then `go mod tidy` and `go build`. That tells the resolver where to find the module content.

sam_support: another CLI approach that helped other customers was to pin the explicit module path with version: `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk@v2.0.0` vs `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2@v2.0.0` — the latter only works if the module published as `/v2`. If module path is wrong you need the replace hack until we cut a correct tag.

acme_sre: thanks. We tried the replace, CI moved past the module error but now runtime fails with `undefined: sdk.NewClient` — looks like API surface changed between tags.

maria_eng: yep possible. If upstream repackaged or introduced breaking changes, you'll either update your imports/usages or pin a previous tag. You can fallback to `v1.7.0` API and keep old code until we cut the proper v2 release with migration docs.

acme_sre: what's the timeline for a proper v2-compatible release? the replace hack is fragile for us.

tom_releasebot: @maria_eng a release request was opened for this repo.

tom_releasebot: creating release branch and CI jobs to verify module path changes.

maria_eng: I'll prioritize. Plan: update module path to include /v2, adjust internal imports, run compatibility tests, then cut v2.1.0 (changelog will note API stability / migration). I expect a patch out in a few hours, will post tag here.

ci_bot: note — GH actions cache may keep the old module. If you still see weird resolution in CI after the new tag, add a workflow step: `- run: go clean -modcache` or purge actions/cache key for modules.

acme_sre: appreciated. once there's a new tag we'll try to move to `github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2@v2.1.0`.

[~2 hours later]
tom_releasebot: release created: v2.1.0 — go.mod updated to `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2` and tagged on the repo. CI jobs ran successful. changelog: "module path bump for proper v2 semantics + minor doc fixes"

acme_sre: tried `go get github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2@v2.1.0` + `go mod tidy` in CI, build now passes and `sdk.NewClient` symbol resolved. thanks! :tada:

sam_support: great to hear. For others running into similar: if you see errors like `module github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/v2: no matching versions` check both the tag and the `module` line in upstream go.mod. Cleans up 90% of the support cases.

maria_eng: followup: we'll add a short migration note in the release notes and a small compatibility test in our release pipeline to ensure future v2 tags include the correct module path.

acme_sre: closing the ticket from our side. thanks everyone! :white_check_mark:
